still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there. The oral is not genericised.

Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent Medicare obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 34.5% ever-used minus 26.2% current leaves 8.3% of adults who used a drug and are off now. Cycled is 16.2 points, or 47% of ever-users: ~13.0 points are current users on at least their second course (~50% of current users) and ~3.2 points cycled and are off again. The other ~5.1 points stopped once and never restarted. That fits one-third one-year persistence and 36–47% one-year restart, with restarts boosted by $49 generics. Flow: 9.0 points of first-time users, 6.5 still on. Of the 7.9 points off in 2030, 4.0 restarted. About 70.7M users out of ~270M adults. Age check: 0.20×14 + 0.33×25 + 0.24×36 + 0.23×28.5 = 26.2. The 65+ band (~62M) has ~17.7M users, double 2030, driven by the July 2031 dementia-risk label for 60+ adults with obesity without CVD. Payer mix: Medicare 27% (~19.1M, of which ~16.6M are 65+ and ~2.5M are disability-eligible; ~7.2M via the dementia-risk code), Medicaid 9% (~6.4M), VA/TRICARE/IHS 3% (~2.1M), so public payers hold 39% (~27.6M) and are the default. Commercial is 18% (~12.7M), legitimate cash (generic, TrumpRx, direct) 38% (~26.9M), and gray or counterfeit 5% (~3.5M, down from 5.2M). Income thirds average 26.2, and the top–bottom gap narrowed from 11 to 8.5 points as $39–69 generics reached the bottom third. The binding limit is now income floor, not price. About 20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in uninsured working-age adults in non-expansion states and in Full Plate households that refuse by choice. Adult obesity is ~32.4%. Pediatric: ~1.8% of under-18s, mostly 12–17 (~3.8% of that band) on generic semaglutide. ~0.3% of 6–11-year-olds are on daily generic liraglutide. ~3.1M children live with a parent who has cycled at least twice.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is the largest single payer, at ~19.1M users through coded indications only. The dementia-risk code, widened in July 2031 to adults 60+ with obesity and no CVD, covers ~7.2M of them, almost all on tirzepatide at its negotiated Medicare price (effective Jan 2032, ~$210 net). FICTIONAL arithmetic: dementia route 7.2M × $210 × 12 ≈ $18.1B; generic semaglutide on other codes 6.5M × ~$45 × 12 ≈ $3.5B; other branded 5.4M × ~$230 × 12 ≈ $14.9B; total ≈ $36.6B a year, up ~23% from $29.7B while users rose ~93%. Medicaid has ~6.4M users: 4.6M on generic at ~$30 net (~$1.7B/yr) and 1.8M branded at ~$245 (~$5.3B/yr), ≈ $6.9B. Growth came through routine preferred-drug-list updates that made generic semaglutide first-line on existing diabetes, CV, CKD and MASH codes. The count of states covering weight loss itself is still 9.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $4–30 a month. Chinese tirzepatide-analogues sell across Southeast Asia, Latin America and Africa. Canadian generics run CAD 40–70. Chinese export licensing on peptide-synthesis reagents (Jul 2031) briefly tightened global API supply, and India has since expanded domestic reagent capacity.
access.note: FICTIONAL. US generic semaglutide (injectable) launched Jan 2032 after compound-patent expiry and Novo's settlement with ANDA filers. Launch cash price was $69–79, briefly held up by tariff costs and reagent shortages, and was $39–59 by Q4 2032 at mass pharmacies, mail-order and TrumpRx, including Novo's authorised generic at $49. Tirzepatide, retatrutide, MariTide and the Wegovy pill stay branded: Zepbound cash $279–349, MariTide $299, retatrutide direct ~$499 (list $1,299), oral starts $149. Employer coverage rose 36% → 40%, mostly 'generic-first' formularies. Metabolic tracks hold ~5.0M of the 12.7M commercial users. Orals fell from ~45% to ~31% of users as weekly generic injections took the low end. The gray market is now mostly 'research-grade' high-dose retatrutide and Indian vials for the uninsured in non-expansion states.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist ~30% driver is realised as an existing product in a new form. Lilly filed a 12 mg high-dose retatrutide sNDA in Feb 2031 on TRIUMPH-HD data (mean ~29% loss at 80 weeks, higher dysesthesia and GI discontinuation), and the FDA approved it in Apr 2032, 14 months later, with a lean-mass monitoring requirement. Amycretin, under review at the start of the step, was approved in Feb 2031 (~22%) with modest uptake. Tirzepatide's dementia sNDA, accepted Sep 2030, was approved Jul 2031 on observational and secondary-endpoint evidence, with a confirmatory RCT still running. US generic semaglutide arrived Jan 2032 through patent expiry plus settlement. Generic tirzepatide is not expected before the mid-2030s. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts are still in phase 3 with no filing. Implant programmes remain phase 1 at most. No oral matches tirzepatide. Oral semaglutide for AUD is under review, with a decision in 2033. Global incretin market ~$165B (2031) on volume, while US semaglutide revenue fell ~60% in 2032.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide 12 mg has the highest GI discontinuation in the class (~14% in TRIUMPH-HD). Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users now triggers elastase testing.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; higher in absolute terms at the 12 mg retatrutide dose.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Exocrine-insufficiency claims keep litigation alive.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; post-2029 filings citing EPI consolidated into a new MDL (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, and ~1.45 in people who have cycled three or more times. The 2031 dementia-label extension roughly quadrupled the number of 60+ users without CVD exposed to this risk. Retatrutide 12 mg shows the largest lean-mass loss in the class.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The tirzepatide 60+ dementia label and the retatrutide 12 mg label recommend baseline DXA. Medicare pays for the DXA code, but uptake is uneven.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The interim FDA observational report (2032) agrees with the 2029 replication: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia vs ~3% in controls, dose-related. TRIUMPH-HD mood-flattening adverse events (~11%) fit the known dose relation. There is still no randomised data. Low-dose 'calm' users have not been studied separately.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FTC warning letters (2032) to three telehealth brands over unsubstantiated 'focus' claims; no rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Gray-market and tariff-shortage interruptions (Feb–Apr 2032) caused a measurable regain cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is tied to EPI in long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Micronutrient monitoring language added to semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The rate holds at ~4.1 vs ~1.9 per 1,000 person-years after year 5 on semaglutide. First tirzepatide 5-year data (2032) are underpowered and inconclusive. Small Danish follow-up suggests partial recovery of elastase within 12 months of stopping, but it is not replicated.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded in 2031 with a warning in the semaglutide SmPC. The FDA added EPI to semaglutide's Warnings and Precautions in Nov 2031. There is no class labelling, and generic semaglutide labels carry the warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Generic pricing makes lifelong adolescent exposure economically trivial. The first pediatric liraglutide bone-density interim (2032) shows no growth deficit at 2 years but lower-than-expected BMD gains; the investigators call it inconclusive.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue. No new action.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Counterfeit branded-pen reports fell after generics launched. Harms have shifted to 'research-grade' high-dose retatrutide, with overdose and dysesthesia presentations. Poison-centre calls are ~3× 2025 levels, down from ~4×.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert retained. Tariff-driven CBP inspection raised seizures of finished products. Personal-importation enforcement is still porous.

food_and_beverage.state: About 45% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~12% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~10%. The class split has blurred as generics reached lower-income zip codes: value packs are shrinking there too, and private-label 'protein-first' lines lead growth at Walmart and Kroger. A small premium segment (heritage grains, butter, full-fat dairy) markets to Full Plate households. Protein ingredient prices are still elevated.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and beer ~9%. Cheap generic semaglutide widened off-label alcohol reduction beyond EAPs. Further distillery consolidation in Kentucky. Non-alcoholic lines keep growing. Full Plate bars and 'drinking suppers' are a small, visible counter-niche in Nashville and Asheville.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down and checks smaller. Small-plate menus are universal. QSR value menus shrank in lower-income markets as generic use spread. A boutique 'unmedicated' segment (long tables, fixed menus, 'Full Plate' certification) is growing in Nashville, Austin and Boise from a tiny base.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting. Sizing distribution keeps shifting downward. Growth in structured athletic wear. A 'natural body' line with generous cuts and no stretch is the Full Plate aesthetic, sold by DTC brands. Resale serves cyclers.

fitness.state: Strength and body-composition scanning keep growing. Medicare-paid DXA for 60+ dementia-label starts feeds a senior strength-class boom at YMCAs and budget gyms. Premium DXA-coaching memberships hold at $250–400 a month.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% in 2032 as generic semaglutide replaced branded fills. Employer coverage recovered to 40%, nearly all generic-first. Adherence differentials persist at mid-sized self-insured firms. Part D base premiums rose again on tirzepatide dementia-route volume despite its negotiated price, and plans are tightening prior authorisation on BMI documentation.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide 12 mg, tirzepatide's dementia franchise and Medicare volume. Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell ~60% in 2032, and Novo leans on its authorised generic, the oral and CagriSema. Amgen's MariTide holds the clinic-administered niche. Indian generic makers with US fill-finish lines and the tariff-favoured Liberty Peptide Works (Columbus, OH) split US generic volume. Tariff compliance and reagent sourcing are new cost lines.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Cheap generics flattened the old income signal. A lean body now says little about class. Muscle still marks the top tier: scanned, coached, retatrutide-high-dose with a trainer. The new readable signal is choice. A soft, full, unmedicated body in an expensive coat reads as deliberate, and a regained body still reads as interruption.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Among 65+ Medicare users in Florida and Arizona retirement counties, weight loss under the dementia code is the default, and refusing it is a family argument. In Columbus-area logistics, generic weekly pens have replaced the plant clinic for many workers. In Nashville and Boise, college-educated 25–40-year-olds in Full Plate circles treat being unmedicated as a principle, the way some treated home birth or unvaccinated children. That makes non-use, not thinness, the new status ambiguity.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter for most households. Full Plate suppers (long tables, bread, second helpings expected, phones and pens left at the door) run weekly in ~2,000 venues. The Bread Alone fasting churches split over whether to join them. School lunch debates now include adolescents on generic semaglutide.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an 'unmedicated' badge alongside 'lean-mass verified'. In metro Nashville it is the more-used filter for under-35s. Desire mismatch remains a common therapy complaint. Couples where one partner buys a 'calm' subscription report new arguments over whether it counts as medication.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the mainstream, appetite is a symptom that costs $49 to manage. In Full Plate culture it is evidence of being fully present, and hunger is aestheticised in photography, cookbooks and music. The MAHA wing frames it as purity and the Unmuted wing as class. The two still fight over whether to welcome people who quit because of side effects.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, dose-related. Roughly 2.5–3M adults now take low-dose generic semaglutide primarily for 'calm', 'focus' or 'craving freedom' rather than weight. They are counted within the 26.2% and have not been studied.
interior_life.framing: Telehealth wellness brands sell it as a feature: 'Quiet' and 'Even' subscriptions ($59–89 a month including generic drug and app) promise freedom from craving, focus and calm. Because the drug is generic and prescribed off-label, ads describe 'programmes', not effects. Clinicians still call blunting a dose-related side effect. Full Plate calls it 'buying a quieter self'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers no longer need to encourage steadiness. Employees buy it, and the 'Quiet' brands sell group plans as EAP add-ons. Sales floors and call centres in Phoenix and Tampa report higher 'Quiet' uptake than warehouses. Metabolic tracks (~5.0M) continue with adherence differentials. The EEOC charges remain unresolved. In creative agencies and some trading desks, admitting a 'calm' subscription is mildly stigmatised as performance-enhancing.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Full Plate has an aesthetic: grain-heavy film photography, long-table supper clubs, loud brass and fiddle revival in Nashville, 'appetite' as a lyrical subject. Unmuted 'off nights' merged into it in Detroit and Baltimore. 'Flat' fiction persists as a genre. Sportsbook handle per account is down further. A craft-cocktail scene survives as Full Plate's rebellion.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Monthly-dose couples still plan around shot dates. Mixed couples (one on, one Full Plate) are a recognised counselling category. 'Calm' subscriptions are now a named factor in libido complaints, and therapists ask about them alongside SSRIs.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Full Plate became a voting identity in the 2032 primaries. 31 congressional candidates, mostly Republican and a handful of progressive Democrats, signed an 'Unmedicated Pledge' against public incretin spending and 'calm' marketing. Older voters on Medicare dementia-code tirzepatide are the most loyal defenders of the drugs. There is still no turnout evidence for a 'sedated electorate'. The drug divide now runs by age more than by zip code.

state.regulatory_posture: There was no new federal or state health-policy action on coverage, premiums or conditioning. The FDA approved routinely: amycretin, the tirzepatide dementia extension, the first generic semaglutide ANDAs and retatrutide 12 mg. It added EPI warnings to semaglutide labels. The FTC sent warning letters on 'focus' marketing but made no rule. Trade policy was the only active lever.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. Medicare's expansion followed the label: the 60+ dementia-risk indication is a coded, medically accepted use, so Part D covers it without Congress. Tirzepatide's IRA-negotiated price took effect Jan 2032 on schedule. Tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. PBM fill data, app logs and clinic administration records still flow to wellness vendors. 'Quiet' subscription apps collect mood check-ins under consumer-app privacy terms, outside HIPAA. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules unchanged. The VA moved to generic semaglutide first-line under a national contract partly filled by Liberty Peptide Works. The Army oral pilot continues. DOT still has not ruled on off-label use among drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs (Mar 2031): 25% on imported incretin APIs and 100% on finished incretin products from firms without US fill-finish. China retaliated with export licensing on peptide-synthesis reagents (Jul 2031). Commerce designated Liberty Peptide Works in Columbus a national-security peptide supplier with a $1.6B DPA Title III loan. Indian makers opened New Jersey and North Carolina fill lines to qualify. The result was a three-month generic shortage in early 2032 and launch prices ~$20 higher than they would otherwise have been, though still under $75. US–India talks continue without a deal.

events.event: Commerce imposes Section 232 tariffs on imported incretin ingredients and finished pens, and lends $1.6B to Columbus-based Liberty Peptide Works as a 'national-security' generic semaglutide maker. China answers in July with export licences on peptide-synthesis reagents.

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk indication to adults 60+ with obesity and no heart disease. Within a year about 7.2M Medicare beneficiaries fill it under the coded indication, making Medicare the largest single payer for incretins.

First US generic semaglutide pens launch after compound-patent expiry and a Novo settlement with ANDA filers. Novo's authorised generic lists at $49. Tirzepatide's negotiated Medicare price takes effect the same month, and a reagent shortage keeps pharmacy shelves thin until April.

Telehealth brands launch 'Quiet' and 'Even' subscriptions bundling low-dose generic semaglutide with mood-tracking apps for calm and craving control. Sign-ups pass 2M by summer, and the FTC sends warning letters over 'focus' claims.
FDA approves a 12 mg high dose of Lilly's retatrutide, 14 months after its Feb 2031 filing, with mean weight loss near 29% and a baseline DXA recommendation. Lilly's direct cash price is $499.

A Full Plate supper in Nashville's Centennial Park seats about 12,000. Thirty-one congressional candidates have signed the movement's 'Unmedicated Pledge' against public incretin spending and 'calm' marketing.

open_tensions: Medicare now pays for ~7.2M older adults to take tirzepatide for dementia prevention on a label whose confirmatory RCT reads out in 2034. This is the population most exposed to the fracture warning, and Part D premiums keep rising while generic semaglutide at $45 cannot legally substitute.

A $49 generic turned access into an income-floor question. The remaining non-users are the uninsured in non-expansion states and the Full Plate households who refuse by choice, and the two groups are politically allied for very different reasons.
Reward blunting is now sold as a product to ~2.5–3M people buying 'calm', with no labelling, no randomised data, mood data held outside HIPAA, and only FTC letters standing in for regulation.

Tariffs and a subsidised national champion keep US generic prices ~$20 above where they would otherwise be and tie supply to US–China reagent politics. Another export-licence squeeze would push cyclers into interruption and regain.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars and a Medicare Card: The Shot Went Generic, and Saying No Became an Identity
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 roughly one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about seventy million people. A third of adults have tried one. Two things changed how the country gets them. In January, semaglutide went generic. The pens that cost $1,349 at list price, and still do on the Wegovy box, now sell for $39 to $59 at chain pharmacies, and Novo sells its own authorised version at $49. Eighteen months earlier, the FDA had extended tirzepatide's dementia-risk claim to adults over sixty with obesity and no heart disease. Medicare covers coded indications, so Congress did not need to act. Within a year about seven million beneficiaries were filling it. Medicare is now the largest single payer for these drugs, and public programmes together pay for nearly two users in five.

None of this came from new law. Congress never reopened the obesity benefit, the 2027 wellness-premium guidance still stands, and Illinois is still the only state that bans adherence-linked premiums. Expansion came through labels, patent clocks and a negotiated Medicare price for tirzepatide that took effect on schedule. Part D premiums rose anyway. Medicare now spends about $36 billion a year on the class. Half of it goes to a dementia-prevention claim whose randomised confirmation is two years away, in older people who already carry a fracture warning.

The one active federal lever was trade. In March 2031 Commerce put tariffs on imported incretin ingredients and finished pens and lent $1.6 billion to Liberty Peptide Works, a fill-finish plant outside Columbus, as a national-security supplier. China responded with export licences on synthesis reagents. Generic launch shelves sat thin until April, and prices settled about twenty dollars above where Indian costs would have put them, still well under seventy-five. The gray market shrank to a few million people, most of them chasing high-dose retatrutide.

That drug is the other news. In April the FDA cleared a 12-milligram retatrutide dose with mean weight loss near 29 per cent, close to surgery, delivered by pen. It costs $499 cash, comes with a recommendation for a baseline bone scan, and has the highest dropout of the class. No new safety signal emerged in the window. The pancreatic-enzyme warning went onto semaglutide labels, including the generics, and the hip-fracture numbers held where they were.

Once the drug was cheap, its quieter effect found a market. Since March, telehealth brands have sold 'Quiet' and 'Even' subscriptions: low-dose generic semaglutide, an app and mood check-ins, marketed as freedom from craving and a calmer mind. Two to three million people buy them, many for reasons other than weight. The FTC sent letters. There is no label, because the drug is old and the use is off-label.

Against all of this, not taking it has become an identity. Full Plate began as supper clubs in Nashville and Boise: long tables, bread, second helpings, pens left at the door. It now has its own photography, its own fiddle bands, an 'unmedicated' filter that is the most-used badge for young Nashville daters, and thirty-one congressional candidates who signed its pledge. Its politics are mixed: MAHA parents, fasting churches, the old Unmuted organisers. They agree on little except refusal.

The drug divide used to run by income. Now it runs by age and by choice. Grandparents in Sarasota are on Medicare-paid tirzepatide to protect their memory. Their adult children buy $49 pens or a calm subscription. Some of their grandchildren eat at long tables and say no.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Kowalczyk, 63, clocks in at six at Liberty Peptide Works in Grove City. He works on the fill line under a blue-and-white banner that says AMERICAN PENS FOR AMERICAN PATIENTS. He inspects cartridges for an hour, then trains two new hires on the capper. He has been on semaglutide since 2027, with two gaps. His company plan wants a BMI of 35 and a prior auth. The Kroger pen is $49, so he pays cash and doesn't argue.

At lunch the break room splits the usual way. The younger line leads eat almost nothing, and one of them taps her 'Even' app to log her mood as a seven. Ray eats half a turkey sandwich and wraps the rest.

At four he drives his wife, Carol, 66, to her bone scan. Her Medicare card covers the tirzepatide under a dementia-risk code because her mother didn't know her own kitchen at the end. The technician says Carol's hip is 'a little soft' and hands her a strength-class flyer for the Y.

Their daughter Dana calls on speaker during the drive home. She is in Nashville, setting tables for Saturday's Full Plate supper, sixty seats and bread from a wood oven. 'You could both just come,' she says. 'Eat like people.' Carol says she'd like to remember Dana's kids' names when she's eighty. Dana goes quiet, then asks about the scan.

At nine Ray pinches his belly and gives himself the Thursday shot. Carol is asleep. The pen in his hand is the kind he capped that morning, maybe one he capped himself.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Indian makers opened New Jersey and North Carolina fill lines to qualify.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: new US fill-finish lines would need construction, FDA site approval and ANDA supplements within roughly ten months of the March 2031 tariff, yet they are already splitting generic volume by January 2032. The same compressed timeline applies to Liberty Peptide Works, which is funded in 2031 and supplying the VA and retail by 2032.

least_plausible_claims.quote: That fits one-third one-year persistence and 36–47% one-year restart, with restarts boosted by $49 generics.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the note's own flow has 6.5 of 9.0 first-time users still on drug, and 15.7 of the 17.6 users from 2030 retained. That is roughly 70–90% retention, not one-third one-year persistence. The $49 generics also existed for only about 12 of the 24 months.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Within a year about 7.2M Medicare beneficiaries fill it under the coded indication, making Medicare the largest single payer for incretins.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: dementia-route users go from 1.6M to 7.2M in a year while plans are tightening prior authorisation on BMI documentation. The label rests on observational evidence, and Medicare is called the 'largest single payer' while legitimate cash is 38% against Medicare's 27%.

rationale.badness: Access broadens and the income gradient narrows (gap 11 to 8.5 points, gray market 5.2M to 3.5M), which offsets harms. Against that, ~7.2M older adults take tirzepatide on a label resting on observational evidence while the hip-fracture HR stays ~1.3 to 1.45. Lifelong adolescent exposure is made 'economically trivial', and 2.5–3M people buy unregulated 'calm' subscriptions with mood data outside HIPAA. Cohesion strain is a Full Plate identity split and intergenerational family arguments, which makes this a recognisably harder society but not a catastrophic one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable to fields and events: adoption 26.2 (+8.6), generic semaglutide in Jan 2032 with a settlement event, Medicare public expansion, the dementia label, 12 mg retatrutide at ~29%, Section 232 tariffs, Full Plate, and the 'Quiet' subscriptions. It is slightly strained by EPI labelling and pediatric BMD hints under 'safety_signal: none', and by the DPA loan and VA contract under 'state_action: none'. mechanism: The label-to-Medicare, patent-to-generic-to-gray-market and tariff-to-shortage chains are shown, but the Liberty and Indian fill-line speed is asserted. The 1.6M to 7.2M dementia jump and the rapid Full Plate scale-up (~2,000 weekly venues, 12,000-seat supper) are thinly supported. Commercial users fall (13.6M to 12.7M) while employer coverage rises 36% to 40%, with no explanation. magnitude: Population figures, age bands, income thirds, payer shares, Medicare and Medicaid spending and approval timings all reconcile and sit inside the envelope. The one real failure is that the user flow implies retention far above the stated one-third persistence.
rationale.generativity: The Ray, Carol and Dana thread is vivid: a capper at Liberty, Carol's 'a little soft' hip scan, Dana setting Full Plate tables, and the closing image of the pen he capped himself.
